title: Unverified Claims — Complete Runtime Evidence Audit
body:
# Unverified Claims — Complete Runtime Evidence Audit

## Purpose

This issue is the complete evidence audit for every claim made during the blank/white/black-screen investigation.

Every numbered claim must be independently verified, rejected, or explicitly left pending. A passing unit test is not proof that the real App path is fixed. A hypothesis must not be treated as a fact.

## Required record for EVERY claim

Status: VERIFIED / REJECTED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / PENDING / SUPERSEDED
Source: exact file + function/class + exact or approximate line
Test: exact test file/name or runtime reproduction
Before: observed pre-fix result
After: observed post-fix result
Evidence: runtime trace, object ID, screenshot SHA, ViewTree, metrics, or commit
Reason: why the evidence proves or disproves the claim
Commit: SHA or N/A
Next action: one concrete action

Never invent a source line. If a source hint below is wrong, record the actual location and explain the discrepancy.

---

# A. Rendering / blank-screen claims

1. Renderer performs normal Activity content traversal only when a content root exists (root_id != 0).
2. root_id == 0 means there is no ViewTree for normal traversal.
3. Without a content root the visible frame can consist mainly of the window background.
4. The reported default window background is #303030.
5. Activity/theme windowBackground can replace that default.
6. Missing setContentView can leave the Activity without its intended content tree.
7. A crash in onCreate before setContentView can leave the content root absent.
8. A crash during setContentView can leave content construction incomplete.
9. An NPE during onCreate can produce blank output.
10. The documented F-NEW-156 observation of 19/25 fresh F-Droid APKs producing blank two-color frames is accurate.
11. The 19/25 figure is supported by project evidence.
12. In the cited cases the first-run exception occurred before or during setContentView.
13. An App can call an Android API that has no bridge in dalvik_engine.cpp.
14. An unbridged API can reach a STUBBED path.
15. The relevant stub path can return null.
16. App code can dereference or unwrap that null.
17. That dereference can generate an NPE.
18. The NPE can propagate to the App boundary.
19. EXC-UNCAUGHT-TOP is the relevant uncaught-exception boundary.
20. With strict mode disabled the runtime can continue after an exception by returning null.
21. Continuing with null can hide the original failure and create a later null dereference.
22. In the cited blank-screen chain setContentView does not complete after the exception.
23. That chain can produce a blank/two-color frame.
24. This chain is not sufficient to claim that every blank screen has the same root cause.
25. An unsupported DEX opcode can stop execution.
26. handle_unimplemented can produce HALTED_OPCODE.
27. An unsupported class can stop execution.
28. Interpreter termination can occur before UI creation completes.
29. A Compose App can produce a blank first frame if the Recomposer is not pumped.
30. Recomposer pumping is required for the affected Compose first-frame path.
31. A Custom View can receive a placeholder instead of real rendering.
32. SurfaceView can use a rendering path that is currently incomplete.
33. OpenGL/GL Apps can fail because Surface/GL support is incomplete.
34. libGDX Apps can fail at createGLSurfaceView.
35. A screenshot can capture a surface different from the actual final Activity surface.
36. Multi-Activity Apps can produce a screenshot of the splash window while another window rendered correctly.
37. A screenshot alone is insufficient proof of final-window rendering.
38. WhatsApp can fail through AppContext.set because of a null return.
39. Sliding-panel layouts can produce near-blank frames.
40. OpenCalculator is a concrete example of the SlidingUpPanelLayout issue.
41. The SlidingUpPanelLayout gravity idiom can produce a near-blank layout.

# B. String.split / Pattern claims

42. Pattern.compile is implemented.
43. Pattern.matcher is implemented.
44. Pattern.split was missing from the relevant bridge before e127a71.
45. The missing Pattern.split bridge falls into the generic stub path.
46. That stub path can return a zero-length array.
47. The zero-length result can cause a downstream AGET failure.
48. Two separate String.split handlers existed.
49. The two String.split handlers can behave differently.
50. Duplicate handlers create a dispatch and maintenance risk.
51. Fixing one String.split handler does not necessarily fix the other.
52. The old String.split implementation did not implement full regex semantics.
53. The old implementation mishandled split using the regex whitespace pattern.
54. The old implementation mishandled split using an escaped pipe pattern.
55. The old implementation mishandled split using a character class such as comma/semicolon.
56. The old implementation only partially supported quoted regex syntax.
57. The old implementation retained trailing empty elements.
58. The final substr push could create trailing empty elements.
59. The old split with an empty delimiter could enter an infinite loop.
60. The infinite-loop mechanism is that find with an empty delimiter returns the current position.
61. An empty delimiter has length zero.
62. Therefore the old loop does not advance start.
63. Unbounded parts growth can cause memory exhaustion/OOM.
64. The old empty-delimiter split path was actually observed to hang or timeout.
65. The reported timeout was approximately five seconds.
66. Pattern.compile slash followed by split lacked a working bridge before the fix.
67. The a|b|c escaped-pipe split returned one element before the fix.
68. The a,b,, split retained trailing empty elements before the fix.
69. After the fix Pattern.split returns a real array.
70. After the fix empty-delimiter split terminates.
71. java_split implements the required Java split semantics for the tested cases.
72. java_split uses std::regex.
73. java_split supports quoted-regex syntax.
74. java_split removes trailing empty elements correctly.
75. java_split handles zero-length matches at the start correctly.
76. java_split handles an empty delimiter without nontermination.
77. The active String.split handler uses java_split.
78. A Pattern.split bridge was added.
79. Direct bridge_to_api tests exercise the relevant split semantics.
80. e127a71 contains the reported split and Pattern.split changes.

# C. Simple Calculator runtime chain

81. Before the split fix Simple Calculator reproduced AGET out of bounds with arr_len=0 and idx=-1.
82. After the split fix that AGET failure no longer occurs.
83. After the split fix Pattern.split returns the expected array.
84. Removing the AGET error did not solve the blank/dark screen.
85. Simple Calculator still produced a dark/blank frame after the split fix.
86. The reported frame background was #303030.
87. The reported screenshot hash was 42d344ffac26.
88. NPE in q9/h.V0 still occurred after the split fix.
89. The NPE occurred later in the execution chain than the split failure.
90. The path after Integer.valueOf constructs a HashSet.
91. The same path constructs an ArrayList.
92. The path calls y8/m.u0(Iterable, I)I.
93. The iterator result was suspected to be null before the NPE.
94. The null-iterator explanation was initially only a hypothesis.
95. ArrayList(int) may fail to register its heap object correctly.
96. ArrayList.add may fail to update or register heap state correctly.
97. ArrayList.iterator may return null.
98. ArrayList.iterator may return an unrelated object.
99. A null element inside the Iterable may be the actual NPE source.
100. HashSet.add may insert a null value unexpectedly.
101. ArrayList.add may insert a null value unexpectedly.
102. The exact null source in u0(Iterable,I) remained unresolved at the reported checkpoint.
103. A direct test of new ArrayList(int) is required.
104. A direct test of add(File.getAbsolutePath) is required.
105. A direct test of iterator through bridge_to_api is required.
106. If the direct iterator test returns null, the ArrayList bridge hypothesis is supported.
107. If the direct iterator test is correct, the ArrayList hypothesis must be rejected or revised.
108. After an ArrayList fix Simple Calculator must be rerun.
109. The first new runtime divergence must be recorded.

# D. Fossify Notes

110. Fossify Notes showed no new THROWABLE-MSG after the split fix.
111. Its screenshot did not change after the split fix.
112. The reported screenshot hash is c3b70dfa3b29.
113. The split fix caused no observed Fossify Notes regression.
114. The split fix produced no observed visual improvement in Fossify Notes.
115. Therefore the split fix was not the generic root cause of Fossify Notes visual failure.

# E. VM / interpreter claims

116. aget on a zero-length array can currently fail to raise AIOOBE.
117. The current aget guard is insufficient for arr_len == 0.
118. aget on null can currently fail to raise the correct NPE.
119. iget on null can currently fail to raise the correct NPE.
120. new-array with a negative size can currently fail to raise the correct exception.
121. invoke-virtual uses class_to_superclass_.find in the relevant path.
122. The result of that find can be used without checking end().
123. Missing end() checking can create an invalid lookup or iterator path.
124. A method-dispatch fallback can execute the wrong method.
125. Such a fallback can cause semantic corruption rather than an immediate visible crash.
126. write_v can silently discard an out-of-bounds write.
127. Silent write discard can hide state corruption.
128. Claims 116-127 require independent regression tests before being VERIFIED.

# F. Source-review completeness

129. Approximately 4,700 of 128,352 C++ lines had been read at the reported checkpoint.
130. That is approximately 3.7 percent of the C++ source.
131. Approximately 100k lines remained unread at that checkpoint.
132. A claim of complete source review was therefore not supported.
133. The full invoke-* switch had not been reviewed.
134. sget/sput had not been fully reviewed.
135. filled-new-array had not been fully reviewed.
136. fill-array-data had not been fully reviewed.
137. The opcode switch paths had not been fully reviewed.
138. throw had not been fully reviewed.
139. monitor had not been fully reviewed.
140. check-cast had not been fully reviewed.
141. try_recursive_invoke had not been fully reviewed.
142. resolve_* had not been fully reviewed.
143. android_shadows.cpp had not been fully reviewed.
144. layout_inflater.cpp had not been fully reviewed.
145. webview_engine.cpp had not been fully reviewed.
146. execution_engine.cpp had not been fully reviewed.
147. The remaining resources implementation had not been fully reviewed.
148. The remaining renderer implementation had not been fully reviewed.
149. The remaining framework implementation had not been fully reviewed.
150. At approximately 500 lines per pass, linear review of the whole tree would require more than 100 passes.
151. Execution-path/source-first investigation is more efficient for the current blank-screen investigation.
152. Each discovered runtime failure should be reproduced before being fixed.
153. Each fix should be rerun after modification.
154. A single successful fix must not be presented as the root cause of the whole blank-screen problem.
155. Closing one link in a failure chain requires documenting the next divergence.
156. Every hypothesis must eventually be VERIFIED or REJECTED with evidence.
157. New regression tests should be reproducible by other developers.
158. Test build commands should be represented in the Makefile/test workflow.
159. Simple Calculator must be rerun after each relevant runtime fix.
160. The final success criterion is an actual runtime visual improvement, not merely a green unit test.

# G. ArrayList / iterator findings

161. arraylist_iterator_regression_test.cpp reproduces working new ArrayList plus add.
162. The same test reports size()==2 correctly.
163. The same test reports iterator() returning an object-less or void value with id=0.
164. This iterator failure is consistent with the Simple Calculator NPE path.
165. An initial iterator fix was attempted and failed to make tests green.
166. An earlier handler intercepts the path before the attempted fix.
167. The earlier handler is around line 28080 / block F-036.
168. F-036 executes before the later iterator handler.
169. The F-036 early return produces a void or object-less result.
170. Therefore the first iterator fix was dead or unreachable for the real dispatch path.
171. The failed fix was reverted.
172. The exact condition or return in F-036 must be identified.
173. The exact runtime handler answering ArrayList.iterator must be identified.
174. The class name alone in the API bridge trace is insufficient to identify the actual handler.
175. The complete ArrayList.iterator dispatch chain must be traced.
176. The actual handler, not an unreachable duplicate handler, must be fixed.
177. The ArrayList regression test must reproduce the failure before the fix.
178. The same regression test must pass after the fix.
179. Simple Calculator must be rerun after the ArrayList fix.
180. The first new divergence after that fix must be recorded.

# H. Precise Simple Calculator bytecode/runtime findings

181. The current Simple Calculator NPE is in method Ll8/j;.r.
182. Ll8/j;.r constructs the storage-path list.
183. The reported failing instruction is invoke-static v2, v8, Lq9/h;->V0(String, char[]).
184. The reported program counter is approximately pc=314.
185. v2 comes from iterator.next().
186. v2 is null at that point.
187. check-cast accepts null rather than rejecting it.
188. V0 then fails because the receiver/this is null.
189. This is supported by a real runtime trace.
190. The reported iterator object is obj#1412.
191. obj#1412 is the HashSet created by l8/j.r.
192. That HashSet is populated with add.
193. HashSet.<init> executes on obj#1412.
194. HashSet.add executes on obj#1412.
195. HashSet.iterator executes on obj#1412.
196. The runtime trace shows __iterator_pos__ == -1 after iterator creation.
197. HashSet.hasNext executes after iterator creation.
198. HashSet.next executes after hasNext.
199. HashSet.next returns null.
200. The runtime chain HashSet.iterator -> hasNext -> next -> null -> V0 is reproducible.

# I. HashSet / shadow-registry hypotheses — MUST BE TESTED

201. HashSet.iterator is answered by a different handler than the heap-backed path.
202. That alternate handler belongs to a shadow layer or registry.
203. The shadow layer stores iterator state separately from the runtime heap.
204. The heap-backed path reads iterator state from the object heap.
205. These two storage paths do not share iterator state correctly.
206. HashSet.iterator creates or returns an iterator without setting __iterator_pos__ on the heap object.
207. pos=-1 is the direct cause of next()==null.
208. HashSet.hasNext uses a different storage or dispatch path from iterator.
209. HashSet.next uses a different storage or dispatch path from iterator.
210. The state mismatch causes HashSet.next to fail to find the stored elements.
211. HashSet.next can therefore return null even when HashSet.add successfully stored elements.
212. If confirmed, the root is a storage/dispatch synchronization bug, not merely a null-value bug.
213. If rejected, the actual cause of next()==null must be identified.
214. A valid fix must not patch only iterator while leaving add, hasNext and next inconsistent.
215. HashSet needs one canonical state representation for this iterator path.
216. The canonical state must be shared consistently by add, iterator, hasNext and next.

# J. Required HashSet reproduction

217. A standalone HashSet regression test must run with the shadow registry enabled.
218. The test must use the same bridge path as Simple Calculator.
219. The test must add at least three elements.
220. The test must call iterator().
221. The test must call hasNext() before the first next().
222. The test must call next() three times.
223. The test must record which element each next() returns.
224. The test must record __iterator_pos__ before and after iterator creation if that is a real runtime field.
225. The test must identify the actual iterator handler or dispatch path.
226. The test must identify the actual hasNext handler or dispatch path.
227. The test must identify the actual next handler or dispatch path.
228. The test must establish whether add and iterator use the same object/state backend.
229. The test must establish whether iterator and next use the same object/state backend.
230. The pre-fix test must reproduce the current iterator-id=0 or next-null failure.
231. If standalone HashSet passes while Calculator fails, the real Calculator path must be compared and the divergence identified.
232. If standalone HashSet fails, investigation must continue through the HashSet/dispatch/state chain.
233. The HashSet test must pass after the correct fix.
234. Simple Calculator must be rerun after the HashSet fix.
235. A valid visual result requires a new screenshot plus ViewTree/metrics and runtime trace.
236. If Calculator remains white or dark, the HashSet fix must not be declared the blank-screen fix.

# K. Repository / evidence claims

237. bac49b5 contains the reported eight earlier fixes.
238. Those fixes include inherited onCreate.
239. Those fixes include ContextThemeWrapper.
240. Those fixes include launch ordering.
241. Those fixes include content-root handling.
242. Those fixes include resolveAttribute.
243. Those fixes include per-Activity theme handling.
244. Those fixes include LayoutParams.
245. Those fixes include the window content parent.
246. e127a71 contains the Java-semantics String.split fix.
247. e127a71 contains the Pattern.split bridge.
248. e127a71 contains the split regression test.
249. The split regression test was green after e127a71.
250. 6d51321 contained the intentionally failing ArrayList iterator regression test.
251. ad6bd0a removed the invalid ArrayList test.
252. Temporary debug changes were reverted.
253. The reported repository state contained only confirmed changes at that checkpoint.
254. There is no valid screenshot proving visual success at the current stage.
255. Therefore visual success remains unverified.
256. An old screenshot hash or background is not new visual evidence.
257. A visual fix requires a new screenshot plus ViewTree/metrics plus runtime trace.

# L. Investigation completeness

258. Approximately 4,700 of 128,352 C++ lines had been read at the latest reported checkpoint.
259. That is approximately 3.7 percent.
260. Approximately 100k lines remained unread at that checkpoint.
261. No claim of complete 128k-line source review is justified.
262. Targeted execution-path/source-first investigation is the intended method.
263. A test is insufficient if it does not reproduce the App's real path.
264. A bridge-only test without the shadow registry can miss the real App dispatch path.
265. ArrayList/HashSet tests therefore need comparison with the shadow-registry-enabled path.
266. Dispatch ordering between duplicate or competing handlers must be audited.
267. An earlier handler can make a later attempted fix dead or unreachable.
268. Every dispatch-related fix must prove that the modified handler actually executes.
269. After every fix both the reproduction test and the real App runtime test must be rerun.
270. The final success criterion remains actual removal of the blank/white/black runtime symptom, not merely a green unit test.

---

# Known source hints

Use these as starting points only. Verify the actual locations.

- Renderer/content-root path: src/runtime/execution_engine.cpp around 2540-2640.
- Exception boundary: dalvik_engine.cpp around 8395-8445.
- handle_unimplemented: dalvik_engine.cpp around 18811.
- Pattern implementation: dalvik_engine.cpp around 22357 onward.
- String.split handlers: dalvik_engine.cpp around 37423 and 40039.
- Suspected ArrayList dispatch: around 28080 / block F-036.
- Calculator bytecode: Ll8/j;.r, failing invoke around pc=314.
- Current HashSet runtime object: obj#1412.
- Earlier blank-screen evidence: docs/MASTER_WORKLIST.md, F-NEW-156.
- Split regression: tests/split_pattern_regression_test.cpp.
- Split fix: e127a71.
- ArrayList iterator test: 6d51321.
- Test removal: ad6bd0a.
- Earlier grouped runtime fixes: bac49b5.

If the actual source location differs, record the actual location and explain why.

# Required final audit summary

Maintain this table:

| Status | Count |
|---|---:|
| VERIFIED | |
| REJECTED | |
| PARTIAL | |
| BLOCKED | |
| PENDING | |
| SUPERSEDED | |

Then report:

Current root cause:
Exact source:
Exact handler:
Reproduction test:
Pre-fix evidence:
Fix commit:
Post-fix evidence:
Current first divergence:
Remaining unverified claims:
Next highest-value test:

Do not write "done", "fixed", "root cause found", or "complete" without numbered claims, source location, reproduction, and evidence supporting the statement.

This issue is an evidence audit, not a success report.
